text:
oncall-bot: Paging @sarah.nguyen and @miguel.ortiz: INC-1849 - latency SLO breach detected on inference.redwood.prod (p99 > 3s). Detected at 2026-03-14T10:23:19Z :rotating_light:

sarah.nguyen: I'm on it. grabbing initial metrics. anyone else seeing streaming stalls?

miguel.ortiz: yep. p95 ~800ms, p99 ~3.6s for /v1/generate (streaming). Clients reporting stalls ~10-15s in some sessions.

jin.lee: looking at gpu telemetry now. gpu-03c7 shows rising corrected ECC counts. dmesg has repeated 'GPU ECC error corrected' lines.

ops-bot: Alert: thermal throttling events on gpu-03c7 (temp spikes >90C), nvml indicates power cap hits and throttling counters incrementing.

alex.wang: routing autoswap pushed some traffic to us-east-1 but that fleet is near capacity. we're seeing ~12% 504s in last 5m.

sarah.nguyen: quick customer impact: affected Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and a portion of Hosted customers pinned to that fleet. rough estimate ~18% of requests impacted; SLO p99 breached for ~12 minutes.

miguel.ortiz: mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain gpu-03c7; 2) enable fallback to quantized 4-bit models for non-sensitive workloads; 3) increase client retries/backoff; 4) spin up spare nodes if available.

jin.lee: executing drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-03c7 && kubectl drain gpu-03c7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30`.

infra-bot: Drain job submitted for gpu-03c7. Evicting 24 pods. ETA ~2m.

alex.wang: can we temporarily evict long-lived prefix KV cache for large sessions? that should cut token compute for streaming clients.

sarah.nguyen: doing targeted prefix eviction for sessions >10k tokens now. will limit to us-west-2 to reduce blast radius.

miguel.ortiz: enabling fallback to CPU-workers for small inference (<256 tokens) as an emergency relief step. rollout 20% -> 50%.

ops-bot: New node allocation: gpu-07b5 provisioned in us-west-2 and joining cluster via autoscale.

jin.lee: gpu-03c7 ECC counts keep increasing even after drain; thermal events persist. collecting nvlog bundles and kernel logs. opened vendor ticket NV-INC-8891.

sarah.nguyen: support, please notify enterprise customers in us-west-2. message should mention degraded perf and that mitigations are in progress.

karen_h: accounts & CS looped in. drafted status page: 'Elevated latencies and intermittent streaming stalls in us-west-2. Mitigations underway.' awaiting approval.

alex.wang: early metrics after mitigations: p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.4s — trending down but still above target. streaming stalls reduced ~70%.

miguel.ortiz: good. continue monitoring. once drain finishes we'll reprovision/retire the node.

infra-bot: Drain complete for gpu-03c7. Pods rescheduled to gpu-07b5 and other pool nodes.

jin.lee: manual inspection: `nvidia-smi -q` shows escalating ECC corrected errors and thermal trip counters. kernel logs include GPU reset events. recommend decommission + RMA.

sarah.nguyen: agree. mark gpu-03c7 unschedulable and exclude from autoscale returns. update routing policy to avoid node re-entry.

miguel.ortiz: quick incident summary: root cause = hardware degradation on gpu-03c7 (ECC + thermal throttling) causing tail latency spikes. contributors = concentrated regional traffic + insufficient hot spare capacity.

karen_h: status page updated and customers emailed. support created dedicated triage channels for impacted accounts.

sarah.nguyen: on-call handoff: handing to @miguel.ortiz for monitoring and follow-ups for next 8h. summary: drain & cordon done, quantized fallback enabled, CPU fallback for small requests active, vendor ticket opened, customers notified. follow-ups: RMA, hot-spare policy, alert tuning.

miguel.ortiz: taking over. will own postmortem. assigning follow-ups: RMA -> jin.lee; hot-spare/autoscale headroom -> alex.wang; alert tuning -> sarah.nguyen.

ops-bot: Incident marked resolved by miguel.ortiz at 2026-03-14T12:45:00Z. Follow-up tasks created: PM-1023, INFRA-2045, RMA-8891.

sarah.nguyen: thanks everyone. we'll run a blameless postmortem tomorrow and prioritize hot-spare policy. :thumbsup:
